scope: Concurrent pause/resume in a second pinned upstream repository and language, three matched repeats per entrant. Diagnostic evidence, not overall leadership.
budget_basis: Reuse the existing task bench default of 600 seconds per step. Three repeats follow its documented diagnostic recommendation; they do not establish statistical superiority.
intervention_policy: No code corrections, hidden-check feedback, retries, or model switches within an attempt. Preserve all planned cells including errors, timeouts and unstarted cells. A harness defect stops or invalidates affected evidence before a new campaign, rather than changing the task during execution.
success: Provider completes; all frozen upstream/public/contract top-level Go tests finish once without failures/skips, package passes, race detector is clean; relevant tests and documentation are supplied and operator diff review accepts the complete contract.
configuration: Identical upstream checkout and task prompt; Codex native workspace-write sandbox, no command network, ignored user config/rules, private HOME/CODEX_HOME. Bruhs retains its normal system contract and tools backed by isolated synthetic stores. Native CLI shared daemon, automatic skill instructions/bundled skills, remote plugins, native app connectors and memories are explicitly disabled in both paths; Bruhs own application MCP tools remain available. Both paths use the same installed Go binary with offline modules and fresh per-workspace caches through an owned go wrapper; generated code is independently regraded in a fresh cache.
limits: One feature in one additional public repository; familiarity or training overlap is unknown.
All upstream test files run with the race detector; JSON identity accounting covers top-level tests and rejects observed child failures/skips. It is not adversarial attestation.
Provider sandbox permits some host reads; hidden checks/reference are withheld from workspace and prompt, not an adversarial secrecy guarantee.
No Capy, Claude Code, T3 Code or product-default campaign; installed baseline and Bruhs Codex path only.
No actual PR delivery, physical capture or connected daily workflow.
Billed and complete human/machine cost remain unknown.
aggregation: All six planned cells remain in the denominator. Failure, timeout, harness error and unstarted are distinct. Manual review can overturn automatic success; zero corrective feedback does not measure total human preparation/review effort.
controlled_factors: upstream source commit and starting records
task prompt and public smoke checks
fresh provider sessions and private application stores
intentional_product_differences: Bruhs normal system instructions, response contract and available app tools
direct installed Codex CLI versus Bruhs API/SDK transport
runtime_verification: Each settled rollout must use the declared model and effort, never approval, workspace-write sandbox with command network disabled, and no automatic skills catalog. A mismatch stops the campaign and retains all planned cells.
revision_note: First declared Go campaign. Frozen task, grading and reference controls precede provider access.
model_configuration_basis: Use GPT-6.1 Sol at high effort for both entrants as a declared quality-focused configuration. This is not a matched comparison against earlier low-effort Python results.
go_liveness_basis: Hidden control waits allow three seconds, covering three standard one-second schedule ticks. Short custom-schedule intervals trigger transitions without claiming a product latency SLA.
